subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted workspace-agent config discovery, or keep agent registration explicit through `agents.list` and `agents.create/update/delete` while routing discovery ergonomics to docs/operator tooling?
rationale: The request adds a new config surface, filesystem scanning, trust boundaries, agent routing precedence, and live reload expectations; repository policy treats config/security/default changes as maintainer-owned product decisions.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Continue using central config and explicit agent RPCs, and leave workspace scanning to external operator tooling unless a narrower missing API is identified.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Define a core `agents.autoDiscover` contract with trusted roots, config schema, precedence, validation, reload semantics, and security tests before implementation.

options.title: Extend Runtime Registration First
options.body: Prioritize zero-restart `agents.create/update/delete` and binding reload behavior before adding glob-based config discovery.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Continue using central config and explicit agent RPCs, and leave workspace scanning to external operator tooling unless a narrower missing API is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-source routing signal on the central agent config and gateway agent-method paths.
